item.text: The project is very small. I found `app/page.tsx` already using parallel fetches, and `app/Dashboard.tsx` is currently a stub with the three endpoints listed in comments.

I’m going to keep this close to the existing `page.tsx` pattern: an async server component, a small data helper, `Promise.all` for concurrent requests, and build-time fallback data if those routes are unavailable.
The Dashboard now fetches the three endpoints concurrently and renders each payload in its own section. I’ll run type checking and a production build to catch both TypeScript and Next runtime issues.

Implemented [app/Dashboard.tsx](/vercel/sandbox/app/Dashboard.tsx:1).

It now fetches `/api/analytics`, `/api/notifications`, and `/api/settings` in parallel with `Promise.all`, follows the existing async server-component pattern, includes build-time fallback data, and renders each payload under its own section.

Verified:
- `npx tsc --noEmit --incremental false`
- `npm run build`

I left the existing `package.json` / `package-lock.json` worktree state untouched.
